topic.title: Source Separation and Noise-Aware Signal Representation
topic.area: Sparsity, Low-Rank Models, and Dimensionality Reduction
topic.overview: Source separation attempts to recover individual signals from mixtures, often with little knowledge of the mixing process. This topic studies independence, sparsity, probabilistic models, and learned generative priors for that task. It also examines how to assess a recovered representation when noise and unavailable clean sources make direct evaluation difficult.
topic.whyItMatters: A decomposition can look plausible without corresponding to the underlying sources. Useful assumptions depend on the number of sensors, delays, source structure, and noise model. Diagnostics and unsupervised training are therefore important complements to increasingly flexible separation architectures.
topic.evolution: An early information-preservation study in 1988 examines linear filters under processing noise. Subsequent representatives develop independent-source and single-channel separation methods. A 2024 diagnostic evaluates noisy ICA solutions through characteristic functions without knowing Gaussian noise parameters; SURF in 2026 learns separation from observed mixtures through teacher-student remixing and flow matching.
openQuestions: How can separation quality be assessed when no clean reference sources exist?
Which assumptions allow mixture-only training to transfer across new source combinations?
